name: James Zou
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Data Science, Stanford University
affiliation: Stanford University (courtesy in CS and EE)

notable_papers.title: FrugalGPT: How to Use LLMs While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
notable_papers.contribution: LLM cascade framework -- learns which combination of LLMs to use per query. 98% cost reduction matching GPT-4 quality. Three strategies: prompt adaptation, LLM approximation, LLM cascade with learned scoring.

notable_papers.title: The complementary contributions of academia and industry to AI research
notable_papers.contribution: 25-year meta-analysis: industry produces higher-impact work, academia more novel work.

notable_papers.title: iSight: Expert-AI co-assessment for immunohistochemistry
notable_papers.contribution: HPA10M dataset + multi-task learning for pathology.

notable_papers.title: Stanford Sleep Bench
notable_papers.contribution: Large-scale polysomnography benchmark; contrastive learning for disease prediction.

notable_papers.title: BUSGen: Foundational Generative Model for Breast Ultrasound
notable_papers.contribution: 3.5M image pretrained generative model for medical imaging.

research_themes: Cost-quality optimization as a first-class concern (FrugalGPT formulates model selection as learned policy)
Cascade and routing architectures with confidence gating
Data-centric AI: data quality, data valuation (Shapley-value methods)
Benchmarking rigor: creates large-scale benchmarks with clear evaluation protocols
AI fairness and bias in healthcare
review_critiques: Missing cost analysis: demands inference cost, latency, and cost-quality tradeoffs
Weak scoring/routing justification: expects formal optimization objective with budget constraints
No baseline comparisons against simpler models: consistently shows small models can match large ones
Distribution shift and concept drift: asks 'what happens when query patterns change?'
Insufficient dataset documentation given data-centric focus
Fairness and bias blind spots: missing demographic subgroup analysis is rejection-level
Complexity tax: wants honest discussion of engineering overhead vs savings
biases: Stanford/Databricks ecosystem bias (collaborates with Matei Zaharia)
Healthcare-first lens: may underweight non-biomedical applications
API-centric worldview: FrugalGPT assumes cloud LLM APIs, air-gapped scenarios outside typical frame
Cost optimization framing: may not fit hard real-time constraints where cost is irrelevant
review_style: Quantitative, demands formal cost-quality Pareto analysis, ablation at each cascade tier, distribution shift testing
